title: Clean Hands Save Lives
paras: Germs are everywhere in a hospital. They are on bed rails, door handles, and phones. Many germs are too small to see, but they can make patients very sick.

The easiest way to stop germs is to clean your hands. Nurses clean their hands before they touch a patient and after they touch a patient. They also clean their hands after they take off their gloves.
You can use hand gel or soap and water. Rub the gel on all parts of your hands until they are dry. If your hands look dirty, wash them with soap and water for at least twenty seconds.
Visitors should clean their hands too. It only takes a few seconds, and it can save a life.
zh: 醫院到處都有細菌，在床欄、門把和電話上，很多小到看不見，卻能讓病人生重病。阻止細菌最簡單的方法是清潔雙手：護理師碰病人前後都要，脫手套後也要。可以用乾洗手或肥皂和水：乾洗手要搓到手的每個地方直到乾；手看起來髒時，用肥皂和水洗至少 20 秒。訪客也要清潔雙手，只要幾秒鐘就可能救一條命。

qs.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Gloves are better than hand gel
Cleaning your hands stops germs in hospitals
qs.why: 整篇都在講清潔雙手可以阻止醫院裡的細菌。

qs.q: When should you wash your hands with soap and water?
qs.why: If your hands look dirty, wash them with soap and water：手看起來髒就用肥皂和水洗。
qs.evidence: If your hands look dirty, wash them with soap and water for at least twenty seconds.

qs.q: Nurses clean their hands after they take off their gloves.
qs.why: 文章說脫手套後也要清潔雙手。
qs.evidence: They also clean their hands after they take off their gloves.

qs.q: "Rub the gel on all parts of your hands." Here "rub" means…
options: move your hands against each other
qs.why: rub 是來回搓揉，把乾洗手搓到整隻手。
qs.evidence: Rub the gel on all parts of your hands until they are dry.

qs.q: What does "They" in "They are on bed rails" refer to?
qs.why: 第一句介紹 germs，第二句 They 延續同一主詞。
qs.evidence: Germs are everywhere in a hospital.

qs.q: Which conclusion is supported by the last paragraph?
options: Only nurses need to clean their hands.
Visitors should clean hospital phones instead of their hands.
Hand-cleaning advice also applies to visitors.
qs.why: 最後一段明說訪客也應清潔雙手。
qs.evidence: Visitors should clean their hands too.

title: Help Us Keep You Safe From Falls
paras: Many patients fall in the hospital. Falls can cause broken bones and head injuries, so we want to keep you safe.
Some medicines can make you dizzy or sleepy. Being in bed for many days can also make your legs weak.

Please follow these tips. Use the call button before you get out of bed, especially at night. Wear the non-slip socks we give you. Keep your glasses and your phone close to your bed. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand up.
If you feel dizzy, sit down right away and call us. We are happy to help you every time.
zh: 很多病人會在醫院跌倒，可能骨折或頭部受傷。有些藥會讓人頭暈或想睡，臥床很多天腿也會變無力。請照做：下床前先按呼叫鈴，尤其是晚上；穿我們給的防滑襪；眼鏡和手機放在床邊；站起來前先在床邊坐一分鐘。覺得頭暈就馬上坐下並叫我們，每次我們都很樂意幫忙。

qs.q: Who is this text for?
qs.why: 文中一直用 you 對病人說話，教病人怎麼防跌。

qs.q: Why can patients' legs become weak?
options: They stay in bed for many days
qs.why: 臥床很多天會讓腿變無力。
qs.evidence: Being in bed for many days can also make your legs weak.

qs.q: What should you do before you stand up?
options: Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute
qs.why: 站起來之前先在床邊坐一分鐘。
qs.evidence: Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand up.

qs.q: Falls in the hospital never cause serious injuries.
qs.why: 文章說跌倒會造成骨折和頭部受傷，和題目相反。
qs.evidence: Falls can cause broken bones and head injuries

qs.q: What does "non-slip" describe about the socks?
options: They are worn only when sleeping.
They help stop feet from sliding.
They are too large to stay on the feet.
qs.why: 防跌建議中的 non-slip 指防滑。
qs.evidence: Wear the non-slip socks we give you.

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest about asking for help?
options: Patients should ask only once during their stay.
Staff expect every patient to stand without help.
Staff welcome patients asking whenever help is needed.
qs.why: every time 表示每次需要都樂意協助。
qs.evidence: We are happy to help you every time.

title: Visiting Information
paras: Welcome to Ward 7B. We know that visits from family and friends help patients feel better.
Visiting hours are from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Only two visitors can be with a patient at one time. Children under twelve must come with an adult.
From 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. is quiet time. Patients need to rest, so please keep your voice low and turn off the TV.
Please do not visit if you have a cold, a cough, or a fever. Clean your hands with the gel at the door when you come in and when you leave. Flowers are not allowed in the intensive care unit.
If you have any questions, please ask at the nurses' station.
zh: 歡迎來到 7B 病房，家人朋友來探望能讓病人感覺好一點。探病時間是早上 10 點到晚上 8 點，每次只能兩位訪客，12 歲以下兒童要有大人陪。下午 2 點到 4 點是安靜時間，病人要休息，請小聲並關掉電視。感冒、咳嗽或發燒請不要來；進出時用門口的乾洗手清潔雙手。加護病房不能帶花。有問題請到護理站問。

qs.q: How many visitors can be with a patient at one time?
qs.why: 一次只能兩位訪客。
qs.evidence: Only two visitors can be with a patient at one time.

qs.q: What happens from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.?
qs.why: 下午 2 點到 4 點是安靜時間。
qs.evidence: From 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. is quiet time.

qs.q: Children under twelve cannot visit.
qs.why: 可以來，只是要有大人陪，所以「不能來」是錯的。
qs.evidence: Children under twelve must come with an adult.

qs.q: Visitors can park for free.
qs.why: 文章完全沒有提到停車。

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: To explain visiting rules for Ward 7B
To advertise a new television programme
qs.why: 全文涵蓋探視時間、人數、安靜時段與清潔規範。

qs.q: What does "not allowed" mean in the sentence about flowers?
qs.why: 此處是在說該單位不准帶花，不是花的價格或大小。
qs.evidence: Flowers are not allowed in the intensive care unit.

title: Tell Us About Your Pain
paras: Pain is not something you have to live with in the hospital. Your nurse will ask about your pain many times a day.
We use a scale from 0 to 10. 0 means no pain, and 10 means the worst pain you can imagine. You can also point to faces on a chart, from a happy face to a crying face.
Tell us where it hurts and what it feels like. Is it sharp, dull, burning, or throbbing? Does it come and go, or is it there all the time?

Please tell us early. Pain is easier to control when it is not too strong. Medicine is not the only way to help. Ice packs, warm packs, music, and changing your position can also make you feel better.
zh: 住院時疼痛不是只能忍，護理師一天會問你好幾次。我們用 0 到 10 分：0 是不痛，10 是能想像最痛的；也可以指表上從笑臉到哭臉的臉。告訴我們哪裡痛、是什麼感覺：刺痛、悶痛、燒灼痛還是抽痛？一陣一陣還是一直痛？請早點說，疼痛不太強的時候比較好控制。除了藥，冰敷、熱敷、音樂和換姿勢也能讓你舒服一點。

qs.q: What is the main message of the text?
options: Tell the nurse about your pain early
Pain is normal, so don't talk about it
qs.why: 文章重點是請病人早點、清楚地說出疼痛。

qs.q: What does 10 mean on the scale?
options: The worst pain you can imagine
qs.why: 10 是你能想像最痛的。
qs.evidence: 10 means the worst pain you can imagine.

qs.q: Why should you tell the nurse early?
options: Medicine is cheaper in the morning
Pain is easier to control when it is not too strong
qs.why: 疼痛不太強時比較好控制。
qs.evidence: Pain is easier to control when it is not too strong.

qs.q: Music can help some patients feel better.
qs.why: 文章把音樂列在讓人舒服一點的方法裡。
qs.evidence: Ice packs, warm packs, music, and changing your position can also make you feel better.

qs.q: What can patients point to as another way to describe pain?
qs.why: 第二段說也可指著表上的表情來表示疼痛。
qs.evidence: You can also point to faces on a chart, from a happy face to a crying face.

qs.q: What does "it" in "Does it come and go" refer to?
qs.why: 前兩句都在詢問疼痛的位置與感覺，所以 it 指疼痛。
qs.evidence: Tell us where it hurts and what it feels like.

title: Your Fasting Blood Test
paras: Your doctor ordered a fasting blood test for tomorrow morning. This test checks your blood sugar and your cholesterol.
Fasting means no food. Please do not eat anything after 8 p.m. tonight. You can drink water, and water is good for you. Please do not drink coffee, tea, juice, or milk.
Ask your nurse about your morning medicines. Some medicines are OK to take with a little water, but some should wait until after the test.
The test is at 7 a.m. It takes about five minutes. After the test, you can eat breakfast right away.
zh: 醫師開了明天早上的空腹抽血，檢查血糖和膽固醇。空腹就是不能吃東西：今晚 8 點後什麼都不要吃。可以喝水，但不要喝咖啡、茶、果汁或牛奶。早上的藥要先問護理師，有些可以配一點水吃，有些要等抽完血。抽血在早上 7 點，大約 5 分鐘，抽完就可以馬上吃早餐。

qs.q: "Fasting means no food." Which is the best meaning of "fasting"?
qs.why: fasting 是一段時間不吃東西（空腹、禁食）。
qs.evidence: Fasting means no food.

qs.q: What can the patient drink before the test?
qs.why: 只可以喝水，咖啡、茶、果汁、牛奶都不行。
qs.evidence: You can drink water, and water is good for you.

qs.q: When can the patient eat?
qs.why: 抽完血就可以馬上吃早餐。
qs.evidence: After the test, you can eat breakfast right away.

qs.q: The patient should not take any medicine in the morning.
qs.why: 文章說有些藥可以配一點水吃，要先問護理師，所以「什麼藥都不能吃」是錯的。
qs.evidence: Some medicines are OK to take with a little water

qs.q: Why should the patient ask about morning medicines?
options: Instructions may differ for different medicines.
The patient must stop every medicine forever.
The test can be replaced by any tablet.
qs.why: 原文說有些藥可配少量水，有些要等檢查後，表示安排不一定相同。
qs.evidence: Some medicines are OK to take with a little water, but some should wait until after the test.

qs.q: What does "ordered" mean in the first sentence?
options: Put all the test results in a row
qs.why: 主詞是醫師、受詞是檢查，表示開立或安排檢查。
qs.evidence: Your doctor ordered a fasting blood test for tomorrow morning.

title: My First Night Shift
paras: Last Friday, I worked my first night shift as a nursing student. It started at eleven at night and finished at seven in the morning.

At night, the ward was very quiet. Most patients were asleep, but the nurses were busy. Every two hours, we checked each patient. We looked at their breathing and their IV lines, and we turned patients who could not move.

At three o'clock, an old man woke up and felt confused. He wanted to go home. He was not like this before, so first my preceptor checked his temperature, blood pressure, oxygen and blood sugar, and she told the doctor on duty. Then she spoke to him softly and turned on a small light. After a few minutes, he felt calm and went back to sleep.
In the morning, I was very tired, but I learned two things: new confusion must be checked and reported, and a calm voice can be strong medicine.
zh: 上週五我以護生身分上了第一個大夜班，晚上 11 點到早上 7 點。晚上病房很安靜，大部分病人在睡，但護理師很忙：每兩小時巡一次病人，看呼吸和點滴，幫不能動的病人翻身。三點時一位老先生醒來意識混亂想回家。他之前不會這樣，所以我的指導護理師先幫他量體溫、血壓、血氧和血糖，也通知值班醫師；接著輕聲跟他說話、開一盞小燈，幾分鐘後他平靜下來又睡著了。早上我很累，但學到兩件事：新出現的意識混亂一定要先評估、通報；冷靜的聲音也可以是一帖良藥。

qs.q: How long was the night shift?
qs.why: 晚上 11 點到早上 7 點，總共 8 小時。
qs.evidence: It started at eleven at night and finished at seven in the morning.

qs.q: How often did they check each patient?
qs.why: 每兩小時巡一次。
qs.evidence: Every two hours, we checked each patient.

qs.q: "He wanted to go home." Who is "he"?
qs.why: 前一句說一位老先生醒來，he 就是他。
qs.evidence: an old man woke up and felt confused

qs.q: What did the writer learn?
options: A calm voice can help patients
Old patients should not stay in hospital
qs.why: 最後一句：冷靜的聲音可以是一帖良藥。
qs.evidence: a calm voice can be strong medicine

qs.q: Which conclusion is supported by the description of the ward?
options: The nurses slept whenever the patients slept.
No patient needed any checks at night.
A quiet ward can still require busy nursing work.
qs.why: 句子把多數病人入睡與護理師忙碌並列。
qs.evidence: Most patients were asleep, but the nurses were busy.

qs.q: What does "calm" mean when the older man felt calm?
qs.why: 他經安撫後回去睡覺，表示情緒平靜，而非仍急著離開。
qs.evidence: After a few minutes, he felt calm and went back to sleep.

qs.q: What did the preceptor do first when the old man became confused?
options: She gave him a sleeping pill.
She checked him and told the doctor on duty.
She called his family to take him home.
qs.why: 他之前不會這樣（新出現的混亂），所以她先量體溫、血壓、血氧和血糖並通知值班醫師，之後才安撫他。新出現的意識混亂可能是譫妄，要先評估、通報。
qs.evidence: first my preceptor checked his temperature, blood pressure, oxygen and blood sugar, and she told the doctor on duty

title: Two Ways to Check Who You Are
paras: In our hospital, every patient wears a wristband. It shows your name and your date of birth.

Before we give you medicine, take your blood, or take you for a test, we will ask you two questions: "What is your name?" and "What is your date of birth?" Then we check your answers against your wristband.
Some patients ask, "Why do you ask me again? You already know me!" We ask every time because many patients have the same or similar names. A small mistake can be very dangerous.
Please help us. Say your full name and your date of birth every time we ask. If your wristband comes off or has the wrong information, tell a nurse right away.
zh: 本院每位病人都戴手圈，上面有姓名和出生日期。給藥、抽血或帶你去檢查前，我們會問你叫什麼名字、出生日期是什麼，再跟手圈核對。有些病人會問：你們不是已經認識我了嗎？我們每次都問，因為很多病人名字一樣或很像，小錯可能很危險。請每次都說出全名和生日；手圈掉了或資料不對，要馬上告訴護理師。

qs.q: What two things are on the wristband?
options: The doctor's name and phone number
qs.why: 手圈上有姓名和出生日期。
qs.evidence: It shows your name and your date of birth.

qs.q: Why do nurses ask every time?
options: It is a new rule this year
Many patients have the same or similar names
qs.why: 很多病人名字一樣或很像。
qs.evidence: many patients have the same or similar names

qs.q: Patients should tell a nurse if their wristband comes off.
qs.why: 手圈掉了要馬上告訴護理師。
qs.evidence: If your wristband comes off or has the wrong information, tell a nurse right away.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this explanation?
options: To tell patients how to change their date of birth
To introduce the hospital's room numbers
To help patients understand repeated identity checks
qs.why: 全文說明核對身分的做法、原因及病人的配合方式。

qs.q: What does "similar names" mean?
options: Names that are almost the same
qs.why: same or similar 對比完全相同與相近的名字。
qs.evidence: We ask every time because many patients have the same or similar names.

qs.q: What are the patient's answers checked against?
qs.why: 第二段最後一句說與手圈資訊核對。
qs.evidence: Then we check your answers against your wristband.

title: Sleeping Well in the Hospital
paras: It can be hard to sleep in the hospital. Machines beep, lights are on, and nurses come in at night.
Nurses need to check you at night, but you can still get good rest. Here are some ideas.

Ask for earplugs or an eye mask. Try not to sleep a lot during the day. Turn off your phone an hour before bed. If pain keeps you awake, tell your nurse. A warm drink without caffeine, like milk, may help you relax.
If you still cannot sleep for many nights, talk to your doctor. Good sleep helps your body heal.
zh: 在醫院可能很難睡：機器嗶嗶響、燈開著、護理師半夜會進來。護理師晚上要巡你，但你還是可以好好休息：要耳塞或眼罩、白天別睡太多、睡前一小時關手機；痛到睡不著要告訴護理師；一杯不含咖啡因的熱飲，像牛奶，可能幫你放鬆。連續很多晚都睡不著就跟醫師說。睡得好能幫助身體復原。

qs.q: What is the text about?
options: Ideas to help patients sleep in the hospital
qs.why: 整篇在給住院睡不好的人建議。

qs.q: When should you turn off your phone?
qs.why: 睡前一小時關手機。
qs.evidence: Turn off your phone an hour before bed.

qs.q: Patients can ask for earplugs.
qs.why: 文章建議可以要耳塞或眼罩。
qs.evidence: Ask for earplugs or an eye mask.

qs.q: What does "awake" mean in the sentence about pain?
qs.why: pain keeps you awake 指疼痛讓人無法睡著。
qs.evidence: If pain keeps you awake, tell your nurse.

qs.q: What does "you" refer to throughout this text?
qs.why: 文章對住院者說明如何休息，也提到請護理師協助。
qs.evidence: Nurses need to check you at night, but you can still get good rest.

qs.q: Which conclusion is supported by the second paragraph?
options: Patients should stop nurses from doing necessary checks.
Rest still matters even when night checks are needed.
Night checks mean that no rest is possible.
qs.why: but 連接「需要夜間檢查」與「仍可好好休息」，並非要求取消檢查。
qs.evidence: Nurses need to check you at night, but you can still get good rest.

title: Contact Precautions: Information for Visitors
paras: The patient in this room has an infection that can spread by touch. The germs can live on skin, on clothes, and on things in the room, such as the bed rails, the TV remote, and the bathroom door.

To protect yourself and other patients, please follow these steps. Clean your hands before you go in. Put on a gown and gloves before you touch the patient or anything in the room. You do not need a mask unless a nurse tells you to wear one.

Before you leave, take off your gloves and gown inside the room and throw them in the bin by the door. Then clean your hands again. Please do not sit on the patient's bed, and do not use the patient's bathroom.

These rules can feel strange, especially for close family. However, they are the best way to stop the infection from spreading to other people in the hospital and to your family at home. If you have any questions, please ask the nurse caring for the patient.
zh: 這間病人的感染會經由接觸傳播，細菌可以留在皮膚、衣服和房間物品上，例如床欄、遙控器和浴室門。為保護你和其他病人：進房前清潔雙手；碰病人或房內任何東西前穿隔離衣、戴手套；除非護理師要求，不需要戴口罩。離開前在房內脫掉手套和隔離衣，丟進門邊的桶子，再清潔雙手。不要坐病人的床，也不要用病人的廁所。這些規定對家人來說可能很奇怪，但這是阻止感染傳給醫院其他人和家裡的人最好的方法。有問題請問照顧病人的護理師。

qs.q: What is the purpose of this text?
options: To explain how visitors can stop an infection from spreading
To tell visitors when they can come
To describe the patient's illness in detail
qs.why: 整篇都在教訪客怎麼做才不會讓感染傳出去。

qs.q: Where should visitors take off their gown?
qs.why: 要在病房裡面脫掉手套和隔離衣。
qs.evidence: take off your gloves and gown inside the room

qs.q: Visitors must always wear a mask in this room.
qs.why: 文章說除非護理師要求，不需要戴口罩。
qs.evidence: You do not need a mask unless a nurse tells you to wear one.

qs.q: The patient will stay in isolation for two weeks.
qs.why: 文章沒說要隔離多久。

qs.q: What does "These rules" in the last paragraph refer to?
options: Rules for booking a hospital appointment
The protective steps explained in the earlier paragraphs
The names of the objects beside the bed
qs.why: These rules 承接前文手部清潔、防護衣手套及離開前的步驟。

qs.q: What does "spreading" mean in the final paragraph?
options: Passing to other people or places
qs.why: 後面接 to other people，指感染傳播給其他人。
qs.evidence: However, they are the best way to stop the infection from spreading to other people in the hospital and to your family at home.

title: Living With Heart Failure
paras: Heart failure does not mean that your heart has stopped. It means that your heart is not pumping as well as it should. Because of this, fluid can build up in your body, especially in your legs and lungs.

The most important thing you can do at home is to weigh yourself every morning. Do it at the same time, after you use the toilet and before you eat breakfast. Write the number in a notebook. A quick weight gain is often the first sign that fluid is building up.

Call your doctor if you gain more than two pounds in one day or five pounds in one week. Also call if your ankles swell, if you need more pillows to breathe at night, or if you feel more tired than usual.

Eat less salt, because salt makes your body hold on to water. Read food labels, and avoid fast food, instant noodles, and canned soup. Take your medicines every day, even when you feel well. If you have chest pain or serious trouble breathing, call 911 right away.
zh: 心臟衰竭不是心臟停了，而是心臟打血不如應有的好，所以水分會積在身體裡，尤其是腿和肺。在家最重要的是每天早上量體重：同一時間、上完廁所、吃早餐前，記在本子上，體重突然增加常是積水的第一個徵兆。一天重了超過 2 磅或一週超過 5 磅要打給醫師；腳踝腫、晚上要墊更多枕頭才能呼吸，或比平常更累也要打。少吃鹽，因為鹽會讓身體留住水；看食品標示，避開速食、泡麵和罐頭湯。每天吃藥，覺得好也要吃。胸痛或嚴重呼吸困難要馬上打 911。

qs.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Why heart failure means the heart has stopped
How to cook food without salt
How people with heart failure can take care of themselves at home
qs.why: 文章教心衰竭病人在家怎麼照顧自己：量體重、少鹽、吃藥、什麼時候求助。

qs.q: When should the patient weigh themselves?
options: Every morning after using the toilet, before breakfast
Once a week at the doctor's office
qs.why: 每天早上、上完廁所、吃早餐前。
qs.evidence: Do it at the same time, after you use the toilet and before you eat breakfast.

qs.q: "Fluid can build up in your body." Here "build up" means…
qs.why: build up 是慢慢累積、越積越多。
qs.evidence: fluid can build up in your body

qs.q: Which sentence explains why patients should eat less salt?
options: "Salt makes your body hold on to water."
qs.why: because 後面就是原因：鹽會讓身體留住水。
qs.evidence: salt makes your body hold on to water

qs.q: What does "the number" in paragraph 2 refer to?
options: The room number at the clinic
The number of pillows in the house
qs.why: 前兩句在說每天固定時間量體重，the number 即體重讀值。

qs.q: What supports the reason for recording weight regularly?
options: A notebook can replace prescribed medicines.
Quick weight gain can be an early sign of fluid building up.
Every change in weight has the same cause.
qs.why: 第二段最後一句直接說快速增重可能是體液累積的早期線索；沒有說所有增重都相同。
qs.evidence: A quick weight gain is often the first sign that fluid is building up.

title: Low Blood Sugar: What to Do
paras: People who take insulin or some diabetes pills can get low blood sugar, which is also called hypoglycemia. This usually means a blood sugar level below 70 mg/dL.
Common signs are shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, and feeling dizzy or confused. Some people become angry or act strangely, so family members may notice it first.

If you think your sugar is low, check it right away. If it is below 70 mg/dL, follow the "rule of 15": eat or drink 15 grams of fast sugar, such as half a cup of fruit juice or regular soda, or three or four glucose tablets. Wait 15 minutes, then check again. If it is still below 70 mg/dL, repeat these steps.

When your sugar is back to normal, eat a small snack with carbohydrates and protein, such as crackers and cheese, if your next meal is more than an hour away. If you are confused or cannot swallow safely, someone should call for help instead of giving you food or drink.
zh: 用胰島素或某些糖尿病藥的人可能低血糖，通常指血糖低於 70 mg/dL（毫克／分升）。常見徵象有發抖、冒汗、心跳快、餓、頭暈或意識混亂；有些人會生氣或行為怪異，家人可能先發現。覺得血糖低就馬上測，低於 70 mg/dL 用「15 法則」：吃或喝 15 克快速吸收的糖，例如半杯果汁或一般汽水，或 3 到 4 顆葡萄糖片；等 15 分鐘再測，還低於 70 mg/dL 就重複。恢復正常後，如果下一餐還要超過一小時，吃一點同時有醣類和蛋白質的點心（例如餅乾配起司）。如果意識混亂或無法安全吞嚥，旁人應該叫救援，而不是餵他吃喝。

qs.q: Which is a sign of low blood sugar?
qs.why: 常見徵象：發抖、冒汗、心跳快、餓、頭暈或混亂。
qs.evidence: Common signs are shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, and feeling dizzy or confused.

qs.q: In the "rule of 15", how long should you wait before checking again?
qs.why: 等 15 分鐘再測。
qs.evidence: Wait 15 minutes, then check again.

qs.q: Family members may notice low blood sugar before the patient does.
qs.why: 有些人會生氣或怪怪的，家人可能先發現。
qs.evidence: so family members may notice it first

qs.q: What should happen if the person cannot swallow safely?
qs.why: 不能安全吞嚥時不要餵，應該叫救援。
qs.evidence: someone should call for help instead of giving you food or drink

qs.q: What is the text mainly intended to explain?
options: Why all diabetes medicines should be stopped
How to recognise low blood sugar and respond to it
How to choose a hospital visiting time
qs.why: 文章依序介紹低血糖、可能徵象及不同情況下的處理。

qs.q: What does "confused" mean in the list of signs?
qs.why: 與行為反常等症狀並列，confused 指思緒不清楚。
qs.evidence: Common signs are shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat, hunger, and feeling dizzy or confused.

title: What Is a Pressure Injury?
paras: A pressure injury, also called a bed sore or a pressure ulcer, is damage to the skin and the tissue under it. It happens when something presses on the same area for a long time and blood cannot flow there well.

Pressure injuries often form over bones, such as the tailbone, the hips, the heels, and the back of the head. Patients who cannot move by themselves, are very thin, or have wet skin are at higher risk.

The first sign is often an area of skin that does not go lighter when you press it gently. On light skin it usually looks red. On darker skin, redness can be hard to see, so the area may look purple, blue or darker than the skin around it, and it may feel warmer, cooler, harder or softer. Later, the skin may break and become an open wound. Deep pressure injuries can take months to heal and can cause serious infections.

Nurses help prevent pressure injuries by changing patients' position regularly, on a schedule that fits each patient's risk, skin and mattress, using special mattresses, keeping the skin clean and dry, and making sure patients get enough protein and fluids. The good news is that most pressure injuries can be prevented.
zh: 壓力性損傷又叫褥瘡或壓瘡，是皮膚和底下組織受損，發生在同一處被壓太久、血液流不過去的時候。常出現在骨頭突出的地方：尾骨、髖部、腳跟和後腦勺；自己不能動、很瘦或皮膚潮濕的病人風險較高。第一個徵象常是一塊輕壓也不會變淡的皮膚：淺膚色通常看起來發紅；深膚色的發紅不容易看出來，可能呈紫色、藍色或比周圍深，摸起來也可能比較熱、比較涼、比較硬或比較軟。之後可能破掉變成開放性傷口；深的要好幾個月才好，還可能造成嚴重感染。護理師會依每位病人的風險、皮膚狀況和床墊，定時幫病人改變姿勢，並使用特殊床墊、保持皮膚清潔乾燥、確保病人有足夠蛋白質和水分。好消息是大部分都可以預防。

qs.q: Where do pressure injuries often form?
options: Over bones, such as the heels and the hips
qs.why: 常出現在骨頭突出的地方，例如尾骨、髖部、腳跟。
qs.evidence: Pressure injuries often form over bones, such as the tailbone, the hips, the heels, and the back of the head.

qs.q: What is often the first sign?
options: Skin that does not turn lighter when pressed gently
qs.why: 第一個徵象：輕壓也不會變淡的皮膚（淺膚色常是發紅，深膚色可能是紫、藍或比周圍深）。
qs.evidence: The first sign is often an area of skin that does not go lighter when you press it gently.

qs.q: Patients with wet skin have a higher risk.
qs.why: 皮膚潮濕的病人風險較高。
qs.evidence: or have wet skin are at higher risk

qs.q: Most pressure injuries cannot be prevented.
qs.why: 文章說大部分都可以預防，和題目相反。
qs.evidence: most pressure injuries can be prevented

qs.q: What does the passage explain?
options: How pressure injuries develop and why prevention matters
How to choose clothes for a hospital visit
Why every skin wound heals at the same speed
qs.why: 全文介紹形成原因、位置、變化與預防。

qs.q: What does "heal" mean in the third paragraph?
options: Become easier to hide under clothes
qs.why: 上下文談傷口恢復可能要幾個月，heal 指癒合。
qs.evidence: Deep pressure injuries can take months to heal and can cause serious infections.

title: SBAR: A Clear Way to Report
paras: When a patient's condition changes, a nurse often has to call a doctor quickly. If the report is long and confusing, important information can be lost. SBAR is a simple way to organize what you say.

S stands for Situation: who you are, which patient you are calling about, and what the problem is right now. B stands for Background: why the patient is in the hospital and any important history. A stands for Assessment: the vital signs and what you think is happening. R stands for Recommendation: what you want the doctor to do, for example, to come and see the patient or to order a test.

Here is a short example. "This is Nurse Lin on 6 West. Mr. Wang in Room 5 has a new fever of 39 degrees. He had bowel surgery two days ago. His heart rate is 115, and his blood pressure is lower than this morning. I am worried about an infection. Could you come and see him?"
Before the call, have the patient's chart, vital signs, and medicine list ready. After the doctor gives an order, read it back to make sure you heard it correctly.
zh: 病人狀況改變時，護理師常要很快打給醫師；報告又長又亂，重要資訊就可能漏掉。SBAR 是整理說話內容的簡單方法：S（狀況）你是誰、哪位病人、現在的問題；B（背景）為什麼住院和重要病史；A（評估）生命徵象和你認為發生什麼事；R（建議）你希望醫師做什麼，例如來看病人或開檢查。例子：6 西林護理師，5 房王先生新發燒 39 度，兩天前做腸道手術，心跳 115，血壓比早上低，擔心感染，可以請你來看他嗎？打電話前準備好病歷、生命徵象和用藥清單；醫師給醫囑後要複誦確認。

qs.q: What does the B in SBAR stand for?
qs.why: B 是 Background，背景。
qs.evidence: B stands for Background

qs.q: In the example, what is the nurse worried about?
qs.why: I am worried about an infection.
qs.evidence: I am worried about an infection.

qs.q: "Read it back" in the last paragraph means…
options: repeat the order to check it
qs.why: read back 是把醫囑複誦一次，確認聽對。
qs.evidence: read it back to make sure you heard it correctly

qs.q: The nurse should prepare the patient's chart before the call.
qs.why: 打電話前要準備好病歷、生命徵象和用藥清單。
qs.evidence: Before the call, have the patient's chart, vital signs, and medicine list ready.

qs.q: Why does the text introduce SBAR?
options: To help nurses organise important information in a report
To replace all spoken reports with a written exam
To describe how to measure every vital sign
qs.why: 第一段說雜亂的報告會遺漏重要資訊，SBAR 可整理表達。

qs.q: Which request would belong in the Recommendation part?
options: Stating why the patient was admitted
Asking the doctor to come and see the patient
qs.why: R 部分說明希望醫師採取的行動，例如來看病人。
qs.evidence: R stands for Recommendation: what you want the doctor to do, for example, to come and see the patient or to order a test.

title: Sudden Confusion in Older Patients
paras: Older patients in the hospital sometimes become confused very suddenly. They may not know where they are, see things that are not there, or be very sleepy during the day and awake at night. This is often delirium.

Delirium is different from dementia. Dementia develops slowly over months or years. Delirium starts over hours or days, and it often gets better and worse during the same day. It is common after surgery and in patients with infections, dehydration, or many new medicines.
Delirium is a medical problem, not just "old age", so nurses should report it to the doctor quickly. The cause must be found and treated.

Simple things can help. Make sure the patient has their glasses and hearing aids. Keep a clock and a calendar in the room. Turn the lights on during the day, and keep the room dark and quiet at night. Family visits and familiar objects, like photos, can also help the patient feel safe.
zh: 住院的長者有時會突然意識混亂：不知道自己在哪、看到不存在的東西，或白天很想睡、晚上醒著，這常是譫妄。譫妄和失智不同：失智是幾個月到幾年慢慢變化；譫妄在幾小時到幾天內出現，同一天內也常好好壞壞，常見於手術後，以及感染、脫水或用了很多新藥的病人。譫妄是醫療問題，不只是老了，護理師要盡快通報醫師，找出原因並治療。簡單的方法有幫助：戴好眼鏡和助聽器、房裡放時鐘和月曆、白天開燈、晚上保持暗和安靜；家人探訪和熟悉的東西如照片也能讓病人安心。

qs.q: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Older patients should not have visitors
Delirium is sudden confusion that needs attention and can be helped
qs.why: 文章說明譫妄是什麼、要通報、以及怎麼幫忙。

qs.q: How is delirium different from dementia?
options: Delirium starts suddenly, over hours or days
qs.why: 譫妄在幾小時到幾天內出現；失智是幾個月到幾年。
qs.evidence: Delirium starts over hours or days

qs.q: Delirium is just a normal part of getting old.
qs.why: 文章說譫妄是醫療問題，不只是老了。
qs.evidence: Delirium is a medical problem, not just "old age"

qs.q: Which can help a patient with delirium?
options: Having a clock and a calendar in the room
Keeping the room bright all night
qs.why: 房裡放時鐘和月曆可以幫助病人。
qs.evidence: Keep a clock and a calendar in the room.

qs.q: What does "familiar" mean in "familiar objects"?
options: Too small for the patient to see
qs.why: 後面的例子是照片，指病人熟悉的物品。
qs.evidence: Family visits and familiar objects, like photos, can also help the patient feel safe.

qs.q: What conclusion about delirium symptoms is supported by paragraph 2?
options: They always remain exactly the same for months.
They occur only while a patient is asleep.
Their severity may change during a single day.
qs.why: gets better and worse during the same day 表示一天內可能起伏。
qs.evidence: Delirium starts over hours or days, and it often gets better and worse during the same day.

title: Your IV Line
paras: An IV is a thin plastic tube that a nurse puts into a vein, usually in your hand or arm. Through it, we can give you fluids, medicines, and sometimes blood.

Most IVs are comfortable, but please tell your nurse right away if you notice pain, swelling, redness, or a cool or wet feeling around the IV site. These can be signs that the IV is not in the vein anymore or that the area is getting irritated.

Be careful when you move. Do not pull on the tubing, and keep the IV bag above the level of your heart when you walk. If the pump beeps, do not try to fix it yourself. Press the call button and a nurse will come.
Your nurse will check the IV site often and change it when needed. When you no longer need fluids or IV medicines, the IV will be taken out. This only takes a few seconds.
zh: 點滴是護理師放進靜脈的細塑膠管，通常在手或手臂，可以透過它給水分、藥物，有時給血。大部分點滴不會不舒服，但如果注射部位疼痛、腫、紅，或摸起來涼涼濕濕的，要馬上告訴護理師，這可能表示管子不在血管裡了或部位受到刺激。移動時要小心：不要拉管子，走路時點滴袋要高於心臟。點滴機響了不要自己弄，按呼叫鈴護理師會來。護理師會常檢查並在需要時更換；不再需要點滴就會拔掉，只要幾秒鐘。

qs.q: What should you do if the pump beeps?
qs.why: 不要自己弄，按呼叫鈴。
qs.evidence: If the pump beeps, do not try to fix it yourself. Press the call button and a nurse will come.

qs.q: A cool or wet feeling around the IV site can be a warning sign.
qs.why: 涼涼濕濕的感覺是要馬上告訴護理師的徵象之一。
qs.evidence: a cool or wet feeling around the IV site

qs.q: "the area is getting irritated" — here "irritated" means…
qs.why: irritated 是受到刺激、發紅疼痛。
qs.evidence: the area is getting irritated

qs.q: Taking out an IV takes about an hour.
qs.why: 拔點滴只要幾秒鐘。
qs.evidence: This only takes a few seconds.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this text?
options: To explain an IV and what patients should report or avoid
To explain how patients can insert their own IV
To compare the prices of different hospital rooms
qs.why: 全文介紹靜脈管路、警訊、移動注意事項與移除。

qs.q: Which conclusion is supported by the final paragraph?
options: Every IV must stay in place for the rest of the patient's life.
The patient should remove the IV whenever the pump makes a sound.
An IV is removed when it is no longer needed for fluids or IV medicine.
qs.why: 最後一段明確交代不再需要相關治療時會移除。
qs.evidence: When you no longer need fluids or IV medicines, the IV will be taken out.

title: Caring for Your Surgical Wound at Home
paras: Your wound needs a little care while it heals. Most surgical wounds heal well in about two weeks, but this can take longer if you smoke or have diabetes.

Keep the dressing clean and dry. Your surgeon will tell you when you can shower. When you are allowed to shower, let the water run over the wound gently and pat it dry with a clean towel. Do not soak in a bath or go swimming until your doctor says the wound has healed.
Always wash your hands before you touch the wound or change the dressing. Do not put creams or powders on the wound unless your doctor tells you to.

Some pain and a little clear fluid are normal for the first few days. Call your doctor if you notice more redness, swelling, warmth, pus, or a bad smell, or if you have a fever over 38 degrees. If your stitches need to be removed, make an appointment for about ten days after surgery, or when your doctor tells you to.
zh: 傷口在癒合時需要一點照顧。大部分手術傷口約兩週會好，但抽菸或有糖尿病可能更久。保持敷料乾淨乾燥，什麼時候可以淋浴由外科醫師決定；可以淋浴時讓水輕輕流過傷口，用乾淨毛巾輕拍擦乾。醫師說癒合前不要泡澡或游泳。碰傷口或換藥前一定要洗手；除非醫師交代，不要塗乳霜或撒粉。頭幾天有些疼痛和少量清澈液體是正常的；更紅、腫、熱、有膿、有臭味，或發燒超過 38 度要打給醫師。需要拆線的話，約手術後十天，或照醫師說的時間預約。

qs.q: Who decides when you can shower?
qs.why: 外科醫師會告訴你什麼時候可以淋浴。
qs.evidence: Your surgeon will tell you when you can shower.

qs.q: A little clear fluid from the wound is normal in the first few days.
qs.why: 頭幾天有些疼痛和少量清澈液體是正常的。
qs.evidence: Some pain and a little clear fluid are normal for the first few days.

qs.q: Which can make healing slower?
qs.why: 抽菸或糖尿病會讓癒合更久。
qs.evidence: this can take longer if you smoke or have diabetes

qs.q: You should put antibiotic cream on the wound every day.
qs.why: 除非醫師交代，不要在傷口上塗東西。
qs.evidence: Do not put creams or powders on the wound unless your doctor tells you to.

qs.q: What is the overall purpose of this passage?
options: To encourage patients to use any cream they already own
To promise that every wound heals on the same day
To explain wound care at home and changes that need medical advice
qs.why: 各段涵蓋清潔保護、觸碰前洗手，以及需要聯絡醫師的變化。

qs.q: What does "dressing" mean in paragraph 2?
options: The clothes worn to an appointment
A sauce added to a meal
A protective covering over a wound
qs.why: 句子談保持傷口覆蓋物清潔乾燥，dressing 在這裡是敷料。
qs.evidence: Keep the dressing clean and dry.

title: The Rights of Medication Safety
paras: Giving medicine is one of a nurse's most important jobs, and mistakes can hurt patients. To prevent errors, nursing students learn the "rights" of medication safety.

The first five are the right patient, the right drug, the right dose, the right route, and the right time. The right patient means checking two identifiers, such as the name and the date of birth. The right route means giving the medicine the correct way, for example by mouth, by injection, or through an IV.

Many hospitals add more rights, such as the right documentation and the patient's right to refuse. After giving a medicine, the nurse must record it. If a patient refuses a medicine, the nurse should find out why, explain the possible risks, and tell the doctor.
Checking the rights only takes a minute, but it protects patients and nurses. If something does not look right, the safest thing to do is to stop and ask.
zh: 給藥是護理師最重要的工作之一，出錯會傷害病人。為了預防錯誤，護生要學給藥安全的「正確」原則。前五個是：正確病人、正確藥物、正確劑量、正確途徑、正確時間。正確病人指核對兩個身分辨識，例如姓名和出生日期；正確途徑指用對的方式給藥，例如口服、注射或靜脈。很多醫院再加上正確記錄和病人拒絕的權利：給藥後要記錄；病人拒絕時要了解原因、說明可能風險並通知醫師。核對只要一分鐘，卻能保護病人和護理師；覺得哪裡不對，最安全的做法是先停下來問。

qs.q: Which is an example of a "route"?
qs.why: 途徑是給藥的方式：口服、注射、靜脈。
qs.evidence: for example by mouth, by injection, or through an IV

qs.q: What should a nurse do if a patient refuses a medicine?
options: Find out why and tell the doctor
Hide it in the patient's food
Give it the next day without asking
qs.why: 要了解原因、說明風險並通知醫師。
qs.evidence: the nurse should find out why, explain the possible risks, and tell the doctor

qs.q: What is the main message of the last paragraph?
options: Stop and ask if something does not look right
qs.why: 最後一段：覺得不對就停下來問。
qs.evidence: the safest thing to do is to stop and ask

qs.q: "two identifiers" means…
options: two pieces of information that show who the patient is
qs.why: identifier 是用來辨認身分的資料，例如姓名和生日。
qs.evidence: checking two identifiers, such as the name and the date of birth

qs.q: What does "The first five" refer to in paragraph 2?
options: The first five patients admitted that day
The first five medicines on a shelf
qs.why: 前段介紹用藥安全的 rights，下一段列出前五項。
qs.evidence: To prevent errors, nursing students learn the "rights" of medication safety.

qs.q: What must a nurse do after giving a medicine?
options: Wait until the next shift to decide which medicine it was
qs.why: 第三段明說給藥後必須記錄。
qs.evidence: After giving a medicine, the nurse must record it.

title: Know the Signs of a Stroke: BE FAST
paras: A stroke happens when blood cannot reach part of the brain, or when a blood vessel in the brain breaks. Brain cells start to die within minutes, so fast treatment is very important.

The letters BE FAST can help you remember the warning signs. B is for Balance: sudden dizziness or trouble walking. E is for Eyes: sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes. F is for Face: one side of the face droops when the person smiles. A is for Arm: one arm drifts down when the person raises both arms. S is for Speech: words are slurred or strange. T is for Time: call 911 right away.
Write down the time the signs started. Doctors need to know this, because some treatments only work if they are given within a few hours.
Do not give the person anything to eat or drink, because their swallowing may not be safe. Stay with them and keep them calm until help arrives.
zh: 中風是血液到不了部分大腦，或腦裡的血管破裂，腦細胞幾分鐘內就開始死亡，所以快速治療非常重要。BE FAST 幫你記警訊：B 平衡——突然頭暈或走路困難；E 眼睛——一眼或兩眼突然看不清；F 臉——笑的時候一邊臉垂下；A 手臂——兩手舉起時一隻往下掉；S 說話——口齒不清或說話怪；T 時間——馬上打 911。把症狀開始的時間記下來，因為有些治療要在幾小時內給才有效。不要給他吃喝，因為吞嚥可能不安全；陪著他、讓他保持冷靜直到救援到達。

qs.q: What does the F in BE FAST stand for?
qs.why: F is for Face：一邊臉垂下。
qs.evidence: F is for Face

qs.q: Why should you write down the time the signs started?
options: The hospital needs it for the bill
Some treatments only work within a few hours
qs.why: 有些治療要在幾小時內給才有效。
qs.evidence: some treatments only work if they are given within a few hours

qs.q: You should give the person water while you wait for help.
qs.why: 文章說不要給吃喝，吞嚥可能不安全。
qs.evidence: Do not give the person anything to eat or drink

qs.q: "words are slurred" — "slurred" means…
options: not clear and hard to understand
qs.why: slurred 是口齒不清。
qs.evidence: words are slurred or strange

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To help readers recognise a possible stroke and get urgent help
To help readers choose food after a routine appointment
To describe a long exercise programme for healthy adults
qs.why: 文章介紹警訊、緊急求助與等候協助時的注意事項。

qs.q: Which fact supports the need to act quickly?
options: A person may need a written appointment card.
The passage gives a list of hospital visiting hours.
Brain cells can start dying within minutes.
qs.why: 首段明確以腦細胞在幾分鐘內開始死亡，說明迅速處理的重要性。
qs.evidence: Brain cells start to die within minutes, so fast treatment is very important.

title: Hands-Only CPR for Adults
paras: If an adult suddenly collapses and is not breathing normally, their heart may have stopped. Every minute without help makes survival less likely, so anyone nearby can make a difference.

First, make sure the area is safe. Tap the person and shout, "Are you OK?" If there is no response, call 911, or ask someone else to call and to bring an AED if there is one nearby. An AED is a small machine that can shock the heart back into a normal rhythm.

Next, start chest compressions. Put the heel of one hand in the center of the chest, put your other hand on top, and push hard and fast, at least two inches (5 cm) deep but not more than about 2.4 inches (6 cm), about 100 to 120 times a minute. Let the chest come back up after each push.

Keep pushing until the AED is ready, the person starts to breathe normally, or trained help takes over. When the AED arrives, turn it on and follow its voice instructions. Stop pushing only when the AED tells you to, and start pushing again right after a shock or when it says no shock is needed.
zh: 成年人突然倒下且沒有正常呼吸，心臟可能已經停了。沒有急救的每一分鐘都讓存活機會變低，所以旁邊任何人都能救命。先確認環境安全，拍拍他大聲問「你還好嗎？」沒反應就打 911，或請別人打並拿附近的 AED；AED 是能電擊讓心臟恢復正常節律的小機器。接著胸部按壓：一手掌根放胸部中央，另一手疊上，用力快速按，至少 2 吋（約 5 公分）、但不超過約 2.4 吋（6 公分）深，每分鐘約 100 到 120 下，每下讓胸部回彈。一直按到 AED 準備好、他恢復正常呼吸或專業人員接手；AED 來了就打開，照語音指示做：只有 AED 叫你停的時候才停手，電擊完或它說不需要電擊，就馬上繼續按壓。

qs.q: What should you do first?
options: Make sure the area is safe
qs.why: 第一步：確認環境安全。
qs.evidence: First, make sure the area is safe.

qs.q: How fast should you push?
qs.why: 每分鐘約 100 到 120 下。
qs.evidence: about 100 to 120 times a minute

qs.q: "collapses" in the first paragraph means…
qs.why: collapse 是突然倒下。
qs.evidence: If an adult suddenly collapses

qs.q: An AED gives voice instructions.
qs.why: AED 打開後照它的語音指示做。
qs.evidence: turn it on and follow its voice instructions

qs.q: Who is the passage mainly trying to guide?
options: Someone nearby when an adult collapses and is not breathing normally
Someone choosing a long-term diet for an adult
A visitor arranging a routine ward appointment
qs.why: 第一段設定成人突然倒下、呼吸不正常的情境，後文說明身旁的人如何反應。

qs.q: What does "it" in "turn it on" refer to?
options: The call button beside a hospital bed
qs.why: 該句先說 AED 到達，接著的 it 指 AED。
qs.evidence: When the AED arrives, turn it on and follow its voice instructions.

qs.q: How deep should you push on an adult's chest?
options: At least two inches, but not more than about 2.4 inches
As deep as you possibly can
qs.why: 成人至少 2 吋（5 公分），但不要超過約 2.4 吋（6 公分）。
qs.evidence: at least two inches (5 cm) deep but not more than about 2.4 inches (6 cm)

qs.q: What should you do right after the AED gives a shock?
options: Wait to see if the person wakes up
Start pushing on the chest again
qs.why: 電擊完馬上繼續按壓，不要停下來等。
qs.evidence: start pushing again right after a shock

title: Eating Well During Chemotherapy
paras: Chemotherapy can change the way food tastes and smells. Many patients feel sick to their stomach, lose their appetite, or get mouth sores. Eating well is still important, because good nutrition helps your body repair itself and fight infection.

Eat small meals five or six times a day instead of three large ones. Choose soft, plain foods, such as rice porridge, eggs, bananas, and crackers. Cold foods often have less smell, so they may be easier to eat.
Drink plenty of fluids between meals, not with them, so you do not feel too full. If you have mouth sores, avoid spicy, salty, or sour food, and use a soft toothbrush.

Take your anti-nausea medicine as the doctor ordered, not only when you already feel sick. Talk to your nurse or a dietitian if you are losing weight. They can suggest high-protein drinks and other ideas.
zh: 化療會改變食物的味道和氣味，很多病人會噁心、沒胃口或口腔破洞，但吃得好還是很重要，營養幫身體修復和對抗感染。一天吃五六次小餐，不要三大餐；選軟、清淡的食物，像稀飯、蛋、香蕉和餅乾；冷的食物味道比較淡，可能比較吃得下。兩餐之間多喝水，不要邊吃邊喝，才不會太飽。口腔破洞時避免辣、鹹、酸，用軟毛牙刷。止吐藥照醫師的時間吃，不要等已經想吐才吃。體重下降就跟護理師或營養師說，他們可以建議高蛋白飲品和其他方法。

qs.q: Why might cold foods be easier to eat?
qs.why: 冷的食物味道比較淡。
qs.evidence: Cold foods often have less smell

qs.q: When should patients drink fluids?
qs.why: 兩餐之間喝，不要邊吃邊喝。
qs.evidence: Drink plenty of fluids between meals, not with them

qs.q: Patients should take anti-nausea medicine only when they already feel sick.
qs.why: 文章說要照醫師的時間吃，不要等想吐才吃。
qs.evidence: not only when you already feel sick

qs.q: "lose their appetite" means…
qs.why: appetite 是胃口；lose their appetite 就是沒胃口。
qs.evidence: lose their appetite

qs.q: Who does "They" in "They can suggest high-protein drinks" refer to?
qs.why: 前一句提到 nurse or a dietitian，They 承接這些專業人員。
qs.evidence: Talk to your nurse or a dietitian if you are losing weight.

qs.q: Which conclusion is supported by the advice about weight loss?
options: Weight loss means all food should be avoided.
A patient must choose every supplement without asking anyone.
A person losing weight should discuss nutrition with a care professional.
qs.why: 文章直接建議體重下降時與護理師或營養師討論。
qs.evidence: Talk to your nurse or a dietitian if you are losing weight.

title: Bedside Handoff
paras: At the end of every shift, nurses give a handoff report to the next nurse. In many hospitals, this happens at the patient's bedside instead of at the nurses' station.

Bedside handoff has several benefits. Both nurses can see the patient together, check the IV lines and the wound, and make sure the room is safe. The patient can also join the conversation, correct mistakes, and ask questions.

However, nurses must protect privacy. If there are visitors in the room, the nurse should ask the patient before talking about personal information. Sensitive information can be shared away from the bedside.
A good handoff is short and organized. Many nurses use a structure such as SBAR, and they finish by asking, "Do you have any questions?" A clear handoff helps prevent mistakes during the next shift.
zh: 每班結束時護理師要交班給下一班，很多醫院在病床邊交，而不是在護理站。床邊交班有幾個好處：兩位護理師可以一起看病人、檢查點滴和傷口、確認環境安全；病人也能加入對話、更正錯誤、提出問題。不過要保護隱私：房裡有訪客時，談個人資訊前先問病人；敏感資訊可以離開床邊再交。好的交班簡短有條理，很多護理師用 SBAR 這類架構，最後問一句「你有沒有問題？」清楚的交班能預防下一班出錯。

qs.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: Handoff reports given at the patient's bedside
How to clean a patient's room
qs.why: 整篇在講床邊交班的好處和要注意的地方。

qs.q: Why can the patient's participation help?
options: The patient can write the report
qs.why: 病人可以加入對話、更正錯誤、提問。
qs.evidence: The patient can also join the conversation, correct mistakes, and ask questions.

qs.q: What should the nurse do if there are visitors in the room?
options: Ask the patient before talking about personal information
qs.why: 談個人資訊前先問病人。
qs.evidence: the nurse should ask the patient before talking about personal information

qs.q: Bedside handoff takes longer than handoff at the nurses' station.
qs.why: 文章沒有比較兩種交班花的時間。

qs.q: What does "sensitive information" mean in paragraph 3?
options: Personal details that need careful privacy protection
Information that is printed in large letters
Details that every visitor should hear immediately
qs.why: 前句強調保護隱私，因此 sensitive 指需要謹慎保護的個人資訊。
qs.evidence: Sensitive information can be shared away from the bedside.

qs.q: What can both nurses do together during bedside handoff?
options: See the patient, check equipment and the wound, and check room safety
Decide that the patient should never ask questions
Avoid looking at the patient until the next shift ends
qs.why: 第二段完整列出兩位護理師可一起確認的事情。
qs.evidence: Both nurses can see the patient together, check the IV lines and the wound, and make sure the room is safe.

title: Getting Ready for a Nursing Job Interview
paras: Many hospitals in the United States interview nurses by video before they make a job offer. For international nurses, the interview is also a test of how clearly they can communicate in English.

Interviewers often ask behavioral questions, such as "Tell me about a time you made a mistake" or "Tell me about a difficult patient." A useful way to answer is the STAR method: describe the Situation, the Task, the Action you took, and the Result.

Prepare three or four real stories from your clinical experience before the interview. Practice telling each story in about two minutes. Focus on what you did and what you learned, not only on what happened.

At the end, you will usually have a chance to ask questions. Good questions show interest, for example, "How long is the orientation for new nurses?" or "What support do you offer international nurses?" Finally, send a short thank-you email the same day.
zh: 很多美國醫院在發聘書前會用視訊面試護理師；對國際護理師來說，面試也在測英文溝通是否清楚。面試官常問行為題，例如「說一次你犯錯的經驗」或「說一位很難照顧的病人」，好用的回答方法是 STAR：情境、任務、你採取的行動和結果。面試前準備三四個真實的臨床故事，每個練到約兩分鐘，重點放在你做了什麼、學到什麼，不只是發生了什麼。最後通常可以發問，好問題能展現興趣，例如新人訓練多久、對國際護理師有什麼支持。當天寄一封簡短的感謝信。

qs.q: What does the A in STAR stand for?
qs.why: A 是你採取的行動（Action）。
qs.evidence: the Action you took

qs.q: How long should each story take?
qs.why: 每個故事練到約兩分鐘說完。
qs.evidence: Practice telling each story in about two minutes.

qs.q: You should send a thank-you email on the same day.
qs.why: 最後一句：當天寄簡短的感謝信。
qs.evidence: send a short thank-you email the same day

qs.q: What is the writer's main advice?
options: Only international nurses need to prepare
Prepare real stories and practice them before the interview
Never ask questions in an interview
qs.why: 全文重點是事先準備真實故事、練習、最後發問與感謝。

qs.q: What does "orientation for new nurses" most likely mean?
options: A holiday that begins after many years of work
A map showing the interviewer's hometown
An introduction and training period for staff starting work
qs.why: 對象是新到職護理師，orientation 指熟悉工作環境與流程的職前訓練。

qs.q: Which approach best matches the advice for telling a clinical story?
options: List only what other people did, without reflecting.
Avoid saying anything about your own role.
Explain your action and what you learned from it.
qs.why: 第三段強調自己的行動與學到的事，不只敘述發生經過。
qs.evidence: Focus on what you did and what you learned, not only on what happened.

title: Your Rights as a Patient
paras: As a patient, you have rights. Knowing them can help you take part in your own care.

You have the right to clear information about your illness, your treatment, and the possible risks and benefits. Before most procedures, a doctor will explain them and ask you to sign a consent form. You may ask questions and take time to decide.

You have the right to privacy. Staff should not share your health information with other people without your permission, except when the law allows it. You also have the right to refuse a treatment, even if your doctor recommends it, after you understand what may happen.

If English is not your first language, you can ask for a medical interpreter. In most US hospitals, this service is free. Family members, especially children, should not be used as interpreters for important medical conversations.
zh: 身為病人你有權利，了解它們能幫你參與自己的照顧。你有權得到清楚的資訊：病情、治療和可能的風險與好處；多數處置前醫師會說明並請你簽同意書，你可以發問、慢慢決定。你有隱私權：除非法律允許，工作人員未經你同意不能把健康資訊告訴別人。你也有權拒絕治療，即使醫師建議，只要你了解可能的後果。英文不是母語的話，可以要求醫療口譯員，大多數美國醫院免費提供；重要的醫療對話不應該請家人，尤其是小孩來翻譯。

qs.q: What can patients do before they sign a consent form?
options: Ask questions and take time to decide
qs.why: 簽之前可以發問、慢慢決定。
qs.evidence: You may ask questions and take time to decide.

qs.q: Patients can refuse a treatment that their doctor recommends.
qs.why: 即使醫師建議，病人了解後果後也有權拒絕。
qs.evidence: You also have the right to refuse a treatment, even if your doctor recommends it

qs.q: Who should NOT be used as interpreters for important conversations?
qs.why: 重要醫療對話不應該請家人，特別是小孩翻譯。
qs.evidence: Family members, especially children, should not be used as interpreters

qs.q: Why does the text describe patient rights?
options: To tell patients never to ask for explanations
To help patients take part in their care
To explain how to prepare a hospital bill
qs.why: 開頭明確說理解權利有助參與自己的照護。
qs.evidence: Knowing them can help you take part in your own care.

qs.q: What does "permission" mean in paragraph 3?
options: A list of medicines used at home
A decision that can never be changed
qs.why: 此處指分享健康資訊的允許或同意。
qs.evidence: Staff should not share your health information with other people without your permission, except when the law allows it.

qs.q: Which statement is supported by the second paragraph?
options: Patients may receive only the treatment name without any explanation.
Patients can expect explanations of possible risks and benefits.
Questions are permitted only after a procedure is complete.
qs.why: 第二段首句列出疾病、治療以及可能風險與好處的清楚資訊。
qs.evidence: You have the right to clear information about your illness, your treatment, and the possible risks and benefits.

title: What Is the NCLEX?
paras: Every nurse who wants to work as a registered nurse in the United States must pass the NCLEX-RN, a national licensing exam. Graduates of nursing programs outside the United States take the same exam as American graduates, in English, and it can be taken at test centers in several other countries.

The NCLEX is a computerized adaptive test. The computer estimates a candidate’s ability from all the scored answers given so far. It uses that estimate and the test plan to choose the next question. The exam can end when the computer has enough information to make a decision, so candidates can answer different numbers of questions. How hard one question feels does not show whether a candidate is passing.

The exam does not mainly test whether you can remember facts. Instead, it focuses on safe, effective care and clinical judgment. Many questions ask what the nurse should do first, which patient to see first, or which finding needs to be reported to the provider. Newer case-study questions follow one patient through several steps, from recognizing important cues to evaluating the results of care.

For international nurses, reading speed matters. A question about priorities may be only a few sentences long, but a case study can include a nurse's notes, vital signs, and lab results. Practicing nursing questions in English, and not only general English, is one of the best ways to prepare.
zh: 想在美國當註冊護理師都要通過 NCLEX-RN 國家執照考試。美國以外護理系的畢業生考同一份英文考試，也可以在其他幾個國家的考場考。NCLEX 採電腦適性測驗。電腦綜合目前所有計分題的作答，估計考生能力，再依能力估計與考試大綱選下一題。收集到足夠資訊作出判定時，考試便可結束，所以每位考生的題數會不同。單題感覺難不難，無法用來判斷是否達到及格標準。考試主要不是考記不記得事實，而是安全有效的照護和臨床判斷：很多題問護理師應該先做什麼、先看哪位病人、哪個發現要通報醫療人員；較新的個案題會跟著一位病人走好幾步，從辨識重要線索到評值照護結果。對國際護理師來說閱讀速度很重要：優先順序題可能只有幾句，但個案題可能有護理紀錄、生命徵象和檢驗值。用英文練護理題，不只練一般英文，是最好的準備方法之一。

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the text?
options: To compare nursing salaries in different countries
To explain what the NCLEX is and how it tests nurses
To teach the history of nursing
qs.why: 全文說明 NCLEX 是什麼、怎麼出題、怎麼準備。

qs.q: What does the computer use to choose the next question?
options: The estimate from scored answers so far and the test plan
Only whether the candidate got the last question right
The same fixed question order for every candidate
qs.why: 電腦綜合目前所有計分題的作答估計能力，再依能力估計和大綱選題。
qs.evidence: The computer estimates a candidate’s ability from all the scored answers given so far. It uses that estimate and the test plan to choose the next question.

qs.q: Everyone who takes the NCLEX answers the same number of questions.
qs.why: 文章說每個人題數不同。
qs.evidence: candidates can answer different numbers of questions

qs.q: According to the last paragraph, what is one of the best ways to prepare?
qs.why: 用英文練護理題是最好的準備方法之一。
qs.evidence: Practicing nursing questions in English, and not only general English, is one of the best ways to prepare.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, "cues" are…
options: important pieces of information about the patient
qs.why: cue 是線索，這裡指病人身上需要注意的重要資訊。
qs.evidence: from recognizing important cues to evaluating the results of care

qs.q: What supports the conclusion that NCLEX preparation involves more than remembering isolated facts?
options: Every question is copied from a list of general English words.
The computer always selects the same question for all candidates.
Case studies ask learners to follow a patient from noticing cues to evaluating care.
qs.why: 第三段說案例題從辨識線索到評估結果，需把資訊連結到判斷，而不只背單一事實。
qs.evidence: Newer case-study questions follow one patient through several steps, from recognizing important cues to evaluating the results of care.

title: Teach-Back: Checking That Patients Understand
paras: Patients often leave the hospital with new medicines, new equipment and a long list of instructions. Many of them nod and say they understand, even when they are unsure, because they feel embarrassed or do not want to take up the nurse’s time. For this reason, asking “Do you understand?” tells the nurse very little. Most people simply answer “yes.”

Teach-back is a simple way to check understanding. After explaining something, the nurse asks the patient to say it again in their own words: “I want to make sure I explained this clearly. Can you tell me how you will take this medicine at home?” The patient can look at a handout while answering, but repeating the nurse’s exact words does not show that the information has been understood.

An important point is that teach-back is not a test of the patient. It checks how well the nurse has explained the information. If the answer is incomplete or wrong, the nurse explains it again in a different way, perhaps with simpler words or a picture, and then asks for teach-back once more.

Teach-back works best when information is given in small parts. Instead of explaining everything just before discharge, the nurse can “chunk and check”: explain one topic, such as when to take a tablet, check understanding, and then move on to the next topic. Because nurses cannot tell which patients will have difficulty, experts recommend using teach-back with every patient, not only with those who seem confused.
zh: 病人出院時常帶著新藥、新器材和一長串注意事項，很多人就算不確定也會點頭說懂，因為不好意思或不想占用護理師的時間，所以問「你懂了嗎？」幾乎看不出什麼，大多數人只會回答「懂」。teach-back（回覆示教）是確認理解的簡單方法：說明完後，請病人用自己的話再說一次，例如「我想確定我有講清楚，可以告訴我你回家後怎麼吃這個藥嗎？」病人可以看著衛教單回答，但只是照唸護理師的話，不代表真的懂。重點是 teach-back 不是在考病人，而是在檢查護理師講得清不清楚；病人答得不完整或不對，就換個方式再說明（例如用更簡單的字或圖），再請病人說一次。資訊要分小段給：不要在出院前一次講完，而是「分段確認」——講一個主題（例如什麼時候吃藥），確認懂了再講下一個。因為護理師看不出哪些病人會有困難，專家建議對每一位病人都用 teach-back，而不是只對看起來搞不清楚的人。（依 AHRQ 健康識能工具包）

qs.q: What is the text mainly about?
options: A way for nurses to check that patients understand instructions
A test that patients must pass before they go home
The reasons why patients forget their medicines
qs.why: 全文介紹 teach-back：請病人用自己的話說一遍，確認衛教有講清楚。

qs.q: Why does the text say that asking “Do you understand?” tells the nurse very little?
options: Patients do not like nurses who ask questions
The question is too difficult for most patients
Patients often answer “yes” even when they are unsure
qs.why: 很多病人不確定也會點頭說懂，所以這個問題看不出真正的理解。
qs.evidence: Many of them nod and say they understand, even when they are unsure

qs.q: Patients are not allowed to look at a handout during teach-back.
qs.why: 文章說病人可以看著衛教單回答，所以敘述和文章相反。
qs.evidence: The patient can look at a handout while answering

qs.q: In paragraph 3, what does “It” refer to in “It checks how well the nurse has explained the information”?
qs.why: 前一句說 teach-back 不是在考病人，It 接著說明 teach-back 檢查的是護理師講得清不清楚。
qs.evidence: It checks how well the nurse has explained the information.

qs.q: In paragraph 4, “chunk and check” means…
options: writing all the instructions on one page
checking the patient’s chart before each shift
giving information in small parts and checking each part
qs.why: 冒號後面解釋：講一個主題、確認理解，再講下一個。
qs.evidence: explain one topic, such as when to take a tablet, check understanding, and then move on to the next topic

qs.q: Which sentence best supports using teach-back with every patient?
options: Repeating the nurse’s exact words shows understanding.
Nurses cannot tell which patients will have difficulty.
Patients often leave the hospital with new equipment.
qs.why: 最後一句說因為看不出誰會有困難，所以建議每位病人都用；「照唸護理師的話就表示懂了」剛好和文章說的相反。
qs.evidence: Because nurses cannot tell which patients will have difficulty, experts recommend using teach-back with every patient

qs.q: Choose the best heading for the 3rd paragraph.
options: Checking the nurse, not testing the patient
qs.why: 第三段說 teach-back 不是考病人，而是檢查護理師講得清不清楚，講不清楚就換個方式再說明。

title: Living Safely with Warfarin: A Patient Leaflet
paras: Warfarin is a blood thinner. It makes your blood take longer to clot, which lowers the risk of dangerous clots in your heart, legs or lungs. Because it affects clotting, the right dose is different for each person, and taking too much or too little can be harmful.

Take warfarin at the same time every day, exactly as prescribed. Never take a double dose to make up for a missed one. If you forget a dose and remember later the same day, take it then; if you do not remember until the next day, call your doctor for advice. You will need regular blood tests called INR tests, which show how quickly your blood clots. Your doctor uses the result to decide whether your dose should change.

Foods that are high in vitamin K, such as spinach, broccoli and other green leafy vegetables, can make warfarin work less well. You do not need to avoid these foods, but try to eat about the same amount each week, and talk to your doctor before you make a big change to your diet. Ask your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new medicine, including aspirin, pain relievers, cold medicines, vitamins or herbal products, and tell every doctor, dentist and pharmacist that you take warfarin.

Call your doctor straight away if you notice signs of bleeding, such as red or brown urine, black or bloody stools, nosebleeds or bleeding gums that will not stop, unusual bruising or a severe headache. If you fall or hit your head, go to the hospital immediately, even if you are not bleeding, because bleeding can happen inside the head. At home, a soft toothbrush and an electric razor can lower your risk of small cuts.
zh: warfarin（可邁丁）是抗凝血藥，讓血液比較慢凝固，降低心臟、腿或肺出現危險血栓的機會；因為會影響凝血，每個人的劑量不同，吃太多或太少都可能有害。每天同一個時間、照醫囑吃；不要為了補漏掉的那次而一次吃兩倍。忘了吃但同一天想起來就補吃；到隔天才想起來，打電話問醫師。要定期抽血驗 INR，看血液凝固得多快，醫師依結果決定要不要調整劑量。菠菜、花椰菜等深綠色葉菜含很多維生素 K，會讓 warfarin 效果變差；不需要完全不吃，但每週盡量吃差不多的量，大改飲食前先問醫師。吃任何新藥前（包括阿斯匹靈、止痛藥、感冒藥、維生素或草藥）先問醫師或藥師，也要告訴每位醫師、牙醫和藥師你在吃 warfarin。出現出血徵象要馬上打給醫師：紅色或褐色的尿、黑色或帶血的大便、止不住的流鼻血或牙齦出血、不尋常的瘀青、劇烈頭痛。跌倒或撞到頭，就算沒有流血也要立刻去醫院，因為可能在頭裡面出血。在家用軟毛牙刷和電動刮鬍刀可以減少小傷口。（依 AHRQ 抗凝血藥病人指引）

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the leaflet?
options: To explain how warfarin was discovered
To persuade patients to stop eating vegetables
To help patients take warfarin safely at home
qs.why: 整份衛教單在說明怎麼安全地吃 warfarin：時間、驗血、飲食、其他藥和出血徵象。

qs.q: What should a patient do if they forget a dose and remember only the next day?
options: Stop taking warfarin for a week
qs.why: 隔天才想起來要打電話問醫師，而且不能一次吃兩倍。
qs.evidence: if you do not remember until the next day, call your doctor for advice

qs.q: Patients who take warfarin must stop eating green leafy vegetables.
qs.why: 文章說不需要避開這些食物，只要每週吃的量差不多。
qs.evidence: You do not need to avoid these foods

qs.q: In paragraph 1, “clot” means…
options: to move quickly around the body
to leave the body through the skin
to become thick and stop flowing, as blood does
qs.why: clot 是凝固、凝成血塊；warfarin 讓血比較慢凝固。
qs.evidence: It makes your blood take longer to clot

qs.q: Why should a patient go to the hospital after hitting their head, even if there is no bleeding?
options: The patient needs an extra dose of warfarin
Bleeding can happen inside the head
The INR test must be repeated at once
qs.why: 文章說撞到頭可能在頭裡面出血，外面看不到。
qs.evidence: because bleeding can happen inside the head

qs.q: The INR test result helps the doctor decide whether to change the dose.
qs.why: 文章說醫師依 INR 結果決定劑量要不要改。
qs.evidence: Your doctor uses the result to decide whether your dose should change.

qs.q: Choose the best heading for the 4th paragraph.
options: Warning signs and when to get help
qs.why: 第四段列出出血徵象、撞到頭要立刻就醫，還有在家怎麼減少小傷口。

title: A Bedside Handoff in SBAR
paras: At the end of a shift, nurses pass important information to the nurse who takes over. Many hospitals use a structure called SBAR: Situation, Background, Assessment and Recommendation. It helps the speaker give information in a clear order and reminds the listener what to ask about. Below is part of a bedside handoff between two nurses.
Situation: “This is Mr. Daniel Ortiz, 72, in bed 14. He had surgery to replace his right hip yesterday. He is awake and talking, but he says his pain is 7 out of 10 when he moves.”

Background: “He has high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. He is allergic to penicillin. His last pain medicine was at 05:00, and he can have another dose at 09:00. He has a urinary catheter, and the surgical team wants him to sit in a chair this afternoon.”

Assessment: “His temperature is 37.4 °C, his pulse is 92 and his blood pressure is 128 over 76. His oxygen level was 95% on room air at 04:00 but 92% when I checked at 06:30, and he was breathing a little faster. His lungs sound clear. His urine output was 30 milliliters an hour overnight. The dressing is dry.”

Recommendation: “Please recheck his oxygen level and breathing in the next half hour and encourage deep breathing. If his oxygen stays below 94%, let the surgical team know. Give his pain medicine at 09:00, before he tries to sit in the chair.”

The receiving nurse then repeats the key points and asks one question: whether the patient has been using his breathing exercise device. Repeating information in this way is a simple check that nothing important has been missed.
zh: 交班時，護理師把重要資訊交給接班的人。很多醫院用 SBAR：Situation 現況、Background 背景、Assessment 評估、Recommendation 建議，讓說的人照清楚的順序講，也提醒聽的人該問什麼。下面是一段床邊交班：現況——72 歲的 Ortiz 先生在 14 床，昨天做右側髖關節置換，清醒能說話，但活動時疼痛 7 分（滿分 10）。背景——有高血壓和第二型糖尿病，對盤尼西林過敏；上一次止痛藥在 05:00，09:00 可以再給；有導尿管，外科團隊希望他今天下午坐到椅子上。評估——體溫 37.4 °C、脈搏 92、血壓 128/76；血氧 04:00 未用氧氣時是 95%，06:30 量是 92%，呼吸也變得有點快；肺音清楚；夜間尿量每小時 30 毫升；傷口敷料是乾的。建議——半小時內再量血氧和呼吸、鼓勵深呼吸；血氧一直低於 94% 就通知外科團隊；09:00 給止痛藥，讓他坐椅子之前先止痛。接班的護理師接著複述重點，並問了一個問題：病人有沒有在用呼吸訓練器。像這樣複述，是確認沒有漏掉重要資訊的簡單方法。（SBAR 依 AHRQ TeamSTEPPS；病例為教學虛構）

qs.q: What does the text mainly show?
options: Why patients with diabetes need surgery
How one nurse hands over a patient using SBAR
How a hip replacement operation is done
qs.why: 第一段說明 SBAR，接著是一段照 SBAR 順序的床邊交班。

qs.q: When can Mr. Ortiz have his next dose of pain medicine?
qs.why: 上一劑在 05:00，下一劑可以在 09:00 給。
qs.evidence: he can have another dose at 09:00

qs.q: Which finding most likely made the nurse recommend rechecking his breathing soon?
options: His oxygen level fell from 95% to 92%.
qs.why: 血氧從 95% 降到 92%，呼吸也變快，所以建議半小時內再評估；敷料乾、體溫 37.4 °C 都不是這個建議的原因。
qs.evidence: His oxygen level was 95% on room air at 04:00 but 92% when I checked at 06:30

qs.q: Mr. Ortiz is allergic to penicillin.
qs.why: 背景裡直接說他對盤尼西林過敏。
qs.evidence: He is allergic to penicillin.

qs.q: The receiving nurse disagrees with the plan for the day.
qs.why: 文章只說接班的人複述重點、問了一個問題，沒有說同不同意。
qs.evidence: The receiving nurse then repeats the key points and asks one question

qs.q: In the Recommendation, “recheck” means…
qs.why: re- 是「再一次」：recheck 是再量一次、再評估一次。
qs.evidence: Please recheck his oxygen level and breathing in the next half hour

qs.q: Choose the best heading for the 1st paragraph.
options: Why nurses use a fixed order for handoffs
qs.why: 第一段說明交班時用 SBAR 這個固定順序的原因：說的人講得清楚，聽的人知道該問什麼。

title: Two Records About a Fall
paras: Source A, from a ward’s fall-prevention guide: All patients receive universal fall precautions, whatever their risk score. Staff show each patient how to use the call light and keep it within reach, keep the bed in a low position with the brakes locked, and make sure the patient wears non-slip footwear. Floors are kept dry and free of clutter, and a night light is left on. Nurses assess fall risk every shift. Patients at high risk are visited at least once an hour, when staff offer help with toileting and check that personal items are within reach.

Source B, an incident note written at 02:40: Mrs. Lin, 81, was found sitting on the floor beside her bed. She had been assessed as high risk on admission because she walks with a frame and takes a sleeping tablet at night. She said she had tried to walk to the bathroom without calling because she “did not want to wake anyone.” She was wearing her own socks without grips. The call light was on the bedside table, out of her reach. The bed was in the low position with the brakes locked. She had last been checked at 00:30.

She denied hitting her head and could move all her limbs. The nurse checked her vital signs, informed the doctor and her daughter, and increased her checks to every hour, with toileting offered at each visit.
zh: 資料 A（病房防跌指引）：不論跌倒風險分數多少，所有病人都採取一般防跌措施：教病人用叫人鈴並放在拿得到的地方、病床放低並固定煞車、穿防滑鞋襪；地板保持乾燥不雜亂，夜間開小夜燈。每一班都評估跌倒風險；高風險病人至少每小時探視一次，協助如廁並確認個人物品拿得到。資料 B（02:40 的事件紀錄）：81 歲的林太太被發現坐在床邊地上。她入院時因為用助行器走路、晚上吃安眠藥，被評為高風險。她說她沒叫人就想自己走去廁所，因為「不想吵醒別人」；她穿的是自己沒有止滑顆粒的襪子；叫人鈴放在床旁桌上，她拿不到；病床是低的、煞車有固定；上一次探視是 00:30。她說沒有撞到頭，四肢都能動。護理師量了生命徵象，通知醫師和她女兒，並把探視改成每小時一次、每次都協助如廁。（防跌措施依 AHRQ《Preventing Falls in Hospitals》；病例為教學虛構）

qs.q: Why is it useful to read the two sources together?
options: To learn how to measure vital signs
To compare what the guide expects with what happened before the fall
To decide which nurse should be punished
qs.why: A 是應該做到的防跌措施，B 是跌倒當時的情況，一起看才知道哪些做到、哪些沒做到。

qs.q: According to Source A, how often should high-risk patients be visited?
qs.why: 資料 A 說高風險病人至少每小時探視一次；「每一班」是評估跌倒風險的頻率。
qs.evidence: Patients at high risk are visited at least once an hour

qs.q: Which precaution from Source A was followed?
options: The call light was within her reach.
The bed was low with the brakes locked.
qs.why: 資料 B 說床是低的、煞車有固定；叫人鈴拿不到、襪子沒有止滑，這兩項都沒做到。
qs.evidence: The bed was in the low position with the brakes locked.

qs.q: Which detail suggests that the hourly visits in Source A were not happening before the fall?
options: She had last been checked at 00:30.
She could move all her limbs.
qs.why: 紀錄寫在 02:40，上一次探視是 00:30，中間超過兩小時，高風險病人應該至少每小時看一次。
qs.evidence: She had last been checked at 00:30.

qs.q: Mrs. Lin said that she had hit her head.
qs.why: 她否認撞到頭，所以敘述和紀錄相反。
qs.evidence: She denied hitting her head

qs.q: In Source B, “denied” means…
options: said that something was not true
qs.why: deny 是否認：她說自己沒有撞到頭。
qs.evidence: She denied hitting her head and could move all her limbs.

qs.q: Choose the best heading for Source A (the 1st paragraph).
options: How to treat a broken hip
Precautions that apply to every patient
What happened on the night of the fall
qs.why: 資料 A 列出不論風險分數、每位病人都要做的防跌措施，以及高風險病人要多做的事。

title: Reading a Day of Nursing Notes
paras: Nursing notes are short, factual records written during a shift. They rarely say “the patient is getting worse” directly; instead, the reader has to compare one entry with the next. The notes below are about Mr. Chen, 68, who was admitted with pneumonia two days ago.

08:00: Alert and oriented. Temperature 37.8 °C, pulse 96, breathing 20 per minute, blood pressure 124/78, oxygen 95% on 2 L/min by nasal cannula. Coughing up yellow sputum. Ate half of his breakfast. Encouraged fluids.

12:00: Says he feels “very tired.” Temperature 38.6 °C, pulse 108, breathing 24 per minute, blood pressure 110/70, oxygen 93% on 2 L/min. Drank only 200 mL since 08:00. Urine dark. Paracetamol given for fever as ordered.

14:30: Daughter reports that he “is not making sense.” Patient unsure of the day and place. Pulse 118, breathing 28 per minute, blood pressure 96/60, oxygen 90% on 2 L/min. Skin warm and flushed. Urine output 40 mL in the last 4 hours. Provider called using SBAR at 14:35; rapid response team arrived at 14:45.
15:30: Blood cultures and lactate taken. IV fluids started as ordered. Oxygen increased to 4 L/min; oxygen level now 94%. Patient transferred to the high-dependency unit. Daughter updated.
zh: 護理紀錄是值班時寫下的簡短、客觀紀錄，很少直接寫「病人變差了」，讀的人要把前後幾筆拿來比較。以下是 68 歲、兩天前因肺炎住院的陳先生：08:00 意識清楚、定向感正常；體溫 37.8 °C、脈搏 96、呼吸每分鐘 20 次、血壓 124/78、鼻導管 2 L/min 下血氧 95%；咳黃痰；早餐吃一半；鼓勵喝水。12:00 說自己「很累」；體溫 38.6 °C、脈搏 108、呼吸 24、血壓 110/70、血氧 93%；08:00 後只喝了 200 mL；尿色深；依醫囑給退燒藥 paracetamol。14:30 女兒說他「講話怪怪的」；不確定今天是哪天、自己在哪裡；脈搏 118、呼吸 28、血壓 96/60、血氧 90%；皮膚溫熱潮紅；過去 4 小時尿量 40 mL；14:35 用 SBAR 通知醫療人員，14:45 快速反應小組到場。15:30 抽血液培養和乳酸；依醫囑開始靜脈輸液；氧氣調到 4 L/min，血氧回到 94%；轉到加護病房前一級的照護病房；已告知女兒。（敗血症徵象對照 CDC 說明；病例為教學虛構）

qs.q: What do the notes mainly describe?
options: A patient whose condition got worse during one shift
A patient who recovered quickly from pneumonia
How to write nursing notes correctly
qs.why: 從 08:00 到 14:30，體溫、脈搏、呼吸上升，血壓和血氧下降，還出現意識混亂，最後轉到更高照護的病房。

qs.q: What did Mr. Chen’s daughter notice at 14:30?
options: He had eaten all of his lunch
qs.why: 14:30 女兒說他講話怪怪的，紀錄也寫他不確定日期和地點。
qs.evidence: Daughter reports that he “is not making sense.”

qs.q: Which change shows that his breathing became faster during the day?
options: His oxygen level stayed at 95% all day.
His breathing rate rose from 20 to 28 per minute.
qs.why: 呼吸次數 08:00 是 20，12:00 是 24，14:30 是 28；另外兩個選項和紀錄不符。
qs.evidence: breathing 28 per minute

qs.q: The provider was called before the rapid response team arrived.
qs.why: 14:35 用 SBAR 通知醫療人員，14:45 快速反應小組才到。
qs.evidence: Provider called using SBAR at 14:35; rapid response team arrived at 14:45.

qs.q: In the 08:00 note, “sputum” is…
options: a kind of medicine for fever
mucus that is coughed up from the lungs
qs.why: sputum 是痰：從肺咳出來的分泌物，肺炎病人常咳黃痰。
qs.evidence: Coughing up yellow sputum.

qs.q: Which information best explains why the provider was called at 14:35 rather than at 12:00?
options: At 08:00 he was coughing up yellow sputum.
At 14:30 he was confused and his blood pressure had fallen to 96/60.
At 12:00 he had already been given paracetamol.
qs.why: 14:30 出現新的意識混亂、血壓降到 96/60、尿量很少，這些變化比 12:00 更嚴重，所以馬上通報。
qs.evidence: Patient unsure of the day and place.

qs.q: Choose the best heading for the 1st paragraph.
options: How to read changes in nursing notes
Why families should write the notes
qs.why: 第一段說護理紀錄很少直接寫「變差」，要把前後幾筆拿來比較，接著介紹病人。

title: Heart Failure at Home: Instructions and a Phone Call
paras: Part 1, from Mrs. Huang’s discharge instructions: Weigh yourself every morning after you use the toilet and before you eat or drink, using the same scale and similar clothing. Write the number down. Call the heart failure clinic if you gain more than 1 kg in a day or more than 2.3 kg in a week, or a different amount if your doctor gives you one. Also call if your ankles or legs become more swollen, or if you become short of breath doing things that were easy before. Take your water tablet every morning, and do not add salt to your food.

Part 2, a clinic nurse’s note of a phone call five days after discharge: Mrs. Huang, 76, reports that her weight was 61.0 kg on Monday and 63.4 kg this morning, Thursday. She says her shoes feel tight and she now sleeps with two extra pillows because she feels breathless lying flat. She admits that she stopped her water tablet on Tuesday because she had to go to the toilet too often during a family visit. She has been eating instant noodles for lunch. No chest pain.

Plan: Advised her to come to the clinic today for an assessment. Explained why the water tablet matters and asked her to explain the plan in her own words; she correctly described when to weigh herself and when to call. Informed the heart failure doctor. Will call her daughter to arrange transport.
zh: 第一部分是黃太太出院衛教：每天早上上完廁所、吃東西喝水之前量體重，用同一台秤、穿差不多的衣服，記下數字。一天增加超過 1 公斤、或一週增加超過 2.3 公斤（或醫師給的數字），就打電話到心衰竭門診；腳踝或小腿腫得更厲害、或做以前很輕鬆的事也會喘，也要打電話。每天早上吃利尿劑（water tablet），食物不要再加鹽。第二部分是出院第五天門診護理師的電話紀錄：76 歲的黃太太說週一體重 61.0 公斤，今天（週四）早上 63.4 公斤；鞋子變緊，平躺會喘，現在要多墊兩個枕頭睡。她承認週二家人來訪時因為一直跑廁所，就停了利尿劑；午餐一直吃泡麵；沒有胸痛。處置：請她今天來門診評估；說明利尿劑的重要，請她用自己的話說一遍計畫，她正確說出什麼時候量體重、什麼時候要打電話；通知心衰竭醫師；會打給她女兒安排接送。（體重和症狀警訊依美國心臟協會與 HealthLinkBC；病例為教學虛構）

qs.q: What do the two parts show when they are read together?
options: How the clinic chooses new medicines
A patient at home who has several of the warning signs listed in her instructions
A patient who followed all of her instructions perfectly
qs.why: 第一部分列出要打電話的警訊，第二部分的體重增加、腳腫和平躺會喘正好都符合。

qs.q: According to Part 1, when should Mrs. Huang weigh herself?
options: Every morning after using the toilet and before eating or drinking
Only when her ankles are swollen
qs.why: 出院衛教說每天早上上完廁所、吃喝之前量。
qs.evidence: Weigh yourself every morning after you use the toilet and before you eat or drink

qs.q: Which detail in Part 2 matches a reason to call in Part 1?
qs.why: 鞋子變緊表示腳腫了，第一部分說腳踝或小腿更腫就要打電話。
qs.evidence: her shoes feel tight

qs.q: What most likely explains her weight gain?
options: She took too many water tablets.
She stopped her water tablet and ate salty food.
She used a different scale on Thursday.
qs.why: 她週二停了利尿劑，午餐又吃很鹹的泡麵，身體容易留住水分；文章沒有說她換了秤。
qs.evidence: She admits that she stopped her water tablet on Tuesday

qs.q: Her weight gain was more than the weekly limit in her instructions.
qs.evidence: her weight was 61.0 kg on Monday and 63.4 kg this morning

qs.q: In Part 2, “breathless” means…
qs.why: breathless 是喘、呼吸困難：她平躺會喘，所以要多墊枕頭。
qs.evidence: she feels breathless lying flat

qs.q: Choose the best heading for the 3rd paragraph.
options: How to cook meals with less salt
What the nurse did after the call
qs.why: 第三段是護理師的處置：請她今天回診、確認她懂、通知醫師、安排接送。
